_comment: The home page's curated shelf. Two groups, twelve entries, and every one of them is checked against the dataset at build time by `deriveShelves` in `lib/landing.ts`: an id that is not in the catalog, an entry LiteSPM cannot install, an entry whose source is not the one declared here, or an entry that depends on a host whose vendor has ended, fails the build. Nothing here may be invented - the id is the catalog's own id, and the use-case line is editorial prose that must not contradict the row's own summary. Each group is one provenance, so the line a reader is shown about where a row came from is true of every row in it.

groups.title: From the publisher's own manifest
groups.blurb: Published in the Official MCP Registry and read from the publisher's own manifest - the capabilities that cover code, documentation, design, data and deploys.

groups.title: Official skills, as the source list marks them
groups.blurb: Skills a source list marks as official. We publish the label the list gives them; we have not audited them, and LiteSPM does not run what it lists.

entries.useCase: Read a repository, open an issue, comment on a pull request - without leaving the agent.
Pull the current library documentation into the agent, so it stops guessing the API.
Bring a Figma design into the agent, where it can turn the file into code.
Search the pages a team writes in Notion, and update the ones the work touches.
Ask about Workers, DNS and logs from inside the agent.
Manage a Postgres project and its branches from the agent.
Read a PDF, pull the tables out of it, merge pages, fill in a form.
Write a Word document with the headings, tables and letterhead the brief asked for.
Build or repair a spreadsheet, with formulas and charts in the cells.
Put a deck together, read one back, or edit the slides that changed.
Give a new interface a deliberate look, instead of a default one.
Open the app you just built in a real browser and check the flow works.
